rationale: R7 produced six deployment-valid scored games, then correctly selected kermit+theCount as the next frozen-priority opponent stack. The worker sent LEAVE for the completed kermit+zoot table but immediately cleared table_id. Subsequent state/destroy events for that departing table therefore failed the epoch admission check and were ignored as foreign. The destroy event is the transition that creates the next table when desired_stack is None, so the campaign remained connected and healthy but could never rotate stacks. R8 retains the departing table as admitted until ISS confirms destroy; destroy then clears table_id and creates the next table.

mechanism: R7 completes the sixth valid kermit+zoot game and frozen quota priority selects kermit+theCount next.
The worker sends table leave because next_stack differs from the current assignment stack.
The worker clears table_id before ISS emits the departing table's terminal state/destroy events.
Epoch admission no longer contains that table id, so those events are persisted as protocol evidence but ignored as foreign.
The destroy handler therefore never runs.
Only the destroy handler creates the next table when desired_stack is None, leaving the connected worker indefinitely idle.

new_epoch.source_commit_rule: bind every active-game authority and evidence bundle to the clean Git HEAD executing R8
